messages:
maria: FYI — we started seeing a bunch of SCIM provisioning failures from Okta after the KMS rekey.
ash: ugh. what are the errors? 403? 400?
maria: mostly 403 when creating service accounts, and an odd validation failure in the SAML response handling path. Okta logs show 'encrypted attribute mismatch'.
jamal: encrypted attribute mismatch... do you mean the encrypted NameID or an encrypted assertion attribute? any logs?
maria: looks like an encrypted attribute inside the SAML assertion (customAttr: external_id), and our decrypt path fails because the JWE 'salt' header in the assertion doesn't match the KMS envelope context we expect.
kevin: can you paste the relevant header? might be a serialization/encoding change post-rotate.
maria: here's the assertion header from Okta (redacted):
```
{"alg":"RSA-OAEP","enc":"A256GCM","kid":"projects/global/cryptoKeys/ri-key-v2","salt":"bVQx2Q3..."}
```
ash: that salt value should match the KMS context used when we encrypted earlier. if KMS rekey created a new key version, we may be missing a compatibility shim.
jamal: are we using envelope encryption with a metadata field for 'salt' or is that generated client-side? our SDK used to generate a nonce, then pass it as context to KMS; if a client lib upgrade changed base64 url vs std encoding it'll mismatch.
maria: good call — customer reported they upgraded their Okta SAML integration addon last night. could be an encoding change.
kevin: quick checks: 1) confirm our KMS decrypt logs show envelope key kid matched; 2) try re-encrypting a test attr with both encodings and see which Okta accepts.
sre-oncall: alert from kms-audit: decrypt attempts for kid projects/global/cryptoKeys/ri-key-v2 returned INVALID_CONTEXT for ~1200 requests starting at 2026-03-21T04:12Z.
maria: that lines up with the deploy window. ash, can you run a local decrypt with both contexts? I can try a repro against staging Okta.
ash: running now.
ash: quick repro — when I base64url-decode salt vs base64-standard decode, one produces different context bytes. our decrypt path uses base64-standard; Okta seems to send urlsafe.
jamal: so two paths: accept both encodings during decrypt, or normalize upstream before encrypting. which is safer short-term?
kevin: short-term: normalize on decrypt to accept urlsafe and std. long-term: coordinate with Okta addon vendor to fix encoding. also add a compatibility flag in our SAML parser so we can roll back.
maria: agreed. I'll open a small PR to normalize salts and add a feature flag behind a config. also creating a mitigation: re-queue failed SCIM events to retry after decrypt normalization change.
ash: PR draft: normalizeSalt(ctx) -> try base64url decode first, then standard; log which branch taken when a mismatch would have occurred.
kevin: add a metric for INVALID_CONTEXT after change so we can validate reduction.
sre-oncall: thumbs up. I'll hold an on-call window for the deploy.
okta-bot: Incident 2026-03-21-47 created: SCIM provisioning failures — okta-integration-team notified.
maria: thanks. I'll coordinate with Okta vendor and send a customer note. tagging @jamal for audit log follow-up to ensure decryption failures are retained for postmortem.
jamal: on it. I'll export KMS audit entries and the SCIM event ids.
maria: plan: (1) merge normalization PR behind feature flag, (2) deploy to staging, run repro and verify KMS INVALID_CONTEXT drops to zero, (3) roll to prod with monitoring, (4) follow up with vendor for fix and add regression test to our SAML e2e harness.
kevin: looks good. keep me posted if we need an immediate key rollback.
ash: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 (draft) — includes test vectors and log examples.
maria: perfect. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
